# CS 27.923 — Rotor drive system and control mechanism tests

> [!summary]
> CS 27.923 is the endurance test of the rotor drive system and control
> mechanism of a small rotorcraft. It is a CS-27 specification, not a CS-E one,
> and the rotorcraft applicant owns it. The test runs for not less than 100
> hours. Three blocks fill it: 60 hours at maximum continuous torque, 30 or 25
> hours at 75% of it, and 10 hours at take-off torque. Each OEI rating
> requested adds runs of its own.

## Requirement

The verbs below are CS-27's own. They bind the rotorcraft applicant, not the
engine applicant. See `## Bearing on this engine` for what reaches CS-E.

| Ref | Obligation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| **(a)** | Each part tested must be in a serviceable condition at the end of the tests. Conduct no intervening disassembly which might affect test results. | Required |
| **(b)** | Test each rotor drive system and control mechanism for not less than 100 hours. Conduct the test on the rotorcraft, and absorb the torque by the rotors to be installed. | Required |
| **(b)** | Other ground or flight test facilities with other appropriate methods of torque absorption may be used, if the conditions of support and vibration closely simulate the conditions that would exist during a test on the rotorcraft. | Permitted |
| **(c)** | Run a 60-hour part of the test at not less than maximum continuous torque and the maximum speed for use with maximum continuous torque. | Required |
| **(c)** | Set the main rotor controls in the position that will give maximum longitudinal cyclic pitch change, to simulate forward flight. Set the auxiliary rotor controls in the position for normal operation under the conditions of the test. | Required |
| **(d)** | Run a 30-hour part of the test at not less than 75% of maximum continuous torque and the minimum speed for use with 75% of maximum continuous torque, with the main and auxiliary rotor controls in the position for normal operation. Where the use of either 30-minute OEI power or continuous OEI power is requested, this part is 25 hours. | Required |
| **(e)** | Run a 10-hour part of the test at not less than take-off torque and the maximum speed for use with take-off torque, with the main and auxiliary rotor controls in the normal position for vertical ascent. | Required |
| **(e)(1)** | For multi-engine rotorcraft for which the use of 2½ minute OEI power is requested, conduct 12 runs during the 10-hour test. | Required if claimed |
| **(e)(1)(i)** | Each run must consist of at least one period of 2½ minutes with take-off torque and the maximum speed for use with take-off torque on all engines. | Required if claimed |
| **(e)(1)(ii)** | Each run must consist of at least one period for each engine in sequence, during which that engine simulates a power failure and the remaining engines are run at 2½-minute OEI torque and the maximum speed for use with 2½-minute OEI torque for 2½ minutes. | Required if claimed |
| **(e)(2)** | For multi-engine turbine-powered rotorcraft for which the use of 30-second and 2-minute OEI power is requested, conduct 10 runs. | Required if claimed |
| **(e)(2)(i)** | Immediately following a take-off run of at least 5 minutes, each power source must simulate a failure, in turn, and apply the maximum torque and the maximum speed for use with 30-second OEI power to the remaining affected drive system power inputs for not less than 30 seconds. Follow that by application of the maximum torque and the maximum speed for use with 2-minute OEI power for not less than 2 minutes. | Required if claimed |
| **(e)(2)(i)** | Conduct at least one run sequence from a simulated flight idle condition. Where the run is conducted on a bench test, conduct the test sequence following stabilisation at take-off power. | Required if claimed |
| **(e)(2)(ii)** | An affected power input includes all parts of the rotor drive system which can be adversely affected by the application of higher or asymmetric torque and speed prescribed by the test. | Statement |
| **(e)(2)(iii)** | This test may be conducted on a representative bench test facility when engine limitations either preclude repeated use of this power or would result in premature engine removal during the test. | Permitted |
| **(e)(2)(iii)** | Make the loads, the vibration frequency and the methods of application to the affected rotor drive system components representative of rotorcraft conditions. The test components must be those used to show compliance with the remainder of the paragraph. | Required |
| **(f)** | Conduct the parts of the test prescribed in (c) and (d) in intervals of not less than 30 minutes. Conduct the part prescribed in (e) in intervals of not less than 5 minutes. | Required |
| **(f)** | The parts of the test prescribed in (c) and (d) may be accomplished either on the ground or in flight. | Permitted |
| **(g)** | At intervals of not more than five hours during the tests prescribed in (c), (d) and (e), stop the engine rapidly enough to allow the engine and rotor drive to be automatically disengaged from the rotors. | Required |
| **(h)** | Under the operating conditions specified in (c), accomplish 500 complete cycles of lateral control, 500 complete cycles of longitudinal control of the main rotors, and 500 complete cycles of control of each auxiliary rotor. | Required |
| **(h)** | A complete cycle involves movement of the controls from the neutral position, through both extreme positions, and back to the neutral position. | Statement |
| **(h)** | The control movements need not produce loads or flapping motions exceeding the maximum loads or motions encountered in flight. | Relief |
| **(h)** | The cycling may be accomplished during the testing prescribed in (c). | Permitted |
| **(i)** | Accomplish at least 200 start-up clutch engagements. | Required |
| **(i)(1)** | Accomplish them so that the shaft on the driven side of the clutch is accelerated. | Required |
| **(i)(2)** | Accomplish them using a speed and method selected by the applicant. | Required |
| **(j)** | For multi-engine rotorcraft for which the use of 30-minute OEI power is requested, make five runs at 30-minute OEI torque and the maximum speed for use with 30-minute OEI torque, in which each engine, in sequence, is made inoperative and the remaining engine(s) is run for a 30-minute period. | Required if claimed |
| **(k)** | For multi-engine rotorcraft for which the use of continuous OEI power is requested, make five runs at continuous OEI torque and the maximum speed for use with continuous OEI torque, in which each engine, in sequence, is made inoperative and the remaining engine(s) is run for a 1-hour period. | Required if claimed |

Four blocks of the schedule are conditional on a rating. Sub-points (e)(1),
(e)(2), (j) and (k) each open "For multi-engine rotorcraft for which the use of"
a named OEI power "is requested" [ext CS 27.923(j)]. Nothing obliges an
applicant to request the rating; once it is requested, the runs are mandatory.
That is the Required if claimed strength, and `## Bearing on this engine`
settles which of the four arise for this engine.

Sub-point (i)(2) leaves the speed and the method of the clutch engagements to
the applicant, but the engagements themselves are mandatory
[ext CS 27.923(i)(2)]. The row is Required for that reason.

The named blocks are stated as parts of the 100 hours of sub-point (b):
"Each rotor drive system and control mechanism must be tested for not less than
100 hours" [ext CS 27.923(b)]. Sub-points (c), (d) and (e) then account for
60 + 30 + 10 hours.

[VERIFY: how the 100 hours of CS 27.923(b) is made up where the 25-hour
reduction of (d) applies. The named blocks then total 95 hours. CS-27 does not
say what fills the remainder, nor whether the OEI runs of (e)(1), (e)(2), (j)
and (k) count towards the total.]

CS-27 publishes no AMC and no GM to point 27.923. A search of CS-27 Amendment 10
for either returns nothing, exactly as it does for point 27.917. The additional
tests of the same rotor drive system are a separate paragraph, [[CS 27.927]].

### How the CS-29 schedule differs

The two paragraphs share a title and a purpose. They do not share a schedule,
and an engine offered to both codes meets two different run programmes.

- **Total duration and structure.** CS-27 asks for "not less than 100 hours"
  [ext CS 27.923(b)], with no cycle structure. CS-29 asks for "at least 200
  hours plus the time required to meet the requirements of sub-paragraphs
  (b)(2), (b)(3) and (k)" [ext CS 29.923(a)], run in ten-hour test cycles
  [ext CS 29.923(a)(1)].
- **Power steps.** CS-27 has three steps: maximum continuous, 75% of it, and
  take-off torque. CS-29 has five: take-off, maximum continuous, 90%, 80% and
  60% of maximum continuous torque [ext CS 29.923(d)], [ext CS 29.923(e)],
  [ext CS 29.923(f)]. The CS-27 step at 75% has no CS-29 equivalent.
- **Take-off run.** CS-27 runs 10 continuous hours at take-off torque
  [ext CS 27.923(e)]. CS-29 alternates 5 minutes at take-off torque with
  5 minutes at idle, for 1 hour [ext CS 29.923(b)(1)]. The CS-29 form exercises
  the clutch and the overrunning clutch; the CS-27 form does not.
- **The OEI reduction.** Both codes shorten one block where 30-minute or
  continuous OEI power is requested. CS-27 cuts the 75% block from 30 hours to
  25 hours [ext CS 27.923(d)]. CS-29 cuts the 60% block from two hours to
  1 hour [ext CS 29.923(f)].
- **2½ minute OEI.** CS-27 adds 12 runs inside the 10-hour take-off block
  [ext CS 27.923(e)(1)]. CS-29 instead replaces "the third and sixth runs" of
  the take-off run [ext CS 29.923(b)(2)].
- **30-second and 2-minute OEI.** CS-27 fixes 10 runs, each following a take-off
  run of at least 5 minutes, with one 2-minute application after the 30-second
  application [ext CS 27.923(e)(2)]. CS-29 fixes no number of runs, attaches
  them to "any one 5-minute power-on run", and asks for **two** 2-minute
  applications after each 30-second application, the second preceded by a
  stabilised period [ext CS 29.923(b)(3)(i)].
- **30-minute and continuous OEI.** CS-27 fixes five runs for each
  [ext CS 27.923(j)], [ext CS 27.923(k)]. CS-29 fixes no number, and instead
  sets a floor: the number of periods "may not be less than the number of
  engines, nor may it be less than two" [ext CS 29.923(k)(3)].
- **Control cycling.** CS-27 counts cycles: 500 lateral, 500 longitudinal and
  500 of each auxiliary rotor [ext CS 27.923(h)]. CS-29 counts frequency and
  dwell: 15 operations each hour through five named thrust positions, each held
  for at least 10 seconds [ext CS 29.923(c)(1)], [ext CS 29.923(c)(3)], and it
  fixes the share of test time spent in each position [ext CS 29.923(i)].
- **Clutch and brake.** CS-27 asks for at least 200 start-up clutch engagements
  [ext CS 27.923(i)]. CS-29 asks for at least 400 clutch and brake engagements
  and prescribes the rotor brake procedure around 40% of maximum continuous
  rotor speed [ext CS 29.923(j)].
- **Four CS-29 runs have no CS-27 counterpart at all**: the engine
  malfunctioning run [ext CS 29.923(g)], the overspeed run
  [ext CS 29.923(h)], the special testing for two or more gear ratios
  [ext CS 29.923(n)], and the operating lubricants regime
  [ext CS 29.923(p)]. The fatigue and service life provision of
  [ext CS 29.923(m)] has none either.

The asymmetry runs one way only. CS-27 asks for nothing that CS-29 does not,
except the 75% power step and the fixed counts of runs and control cycles.

## Bearing on this engine

CS 27.923 creates no CS-E obligation. The test is run on the rotor drive system
and the control mechanism, which are not part of the engine type design. The
schedule still consumes engine ratings, and the engine applicant supplies them.

Every block is set as a torque, with a named rotational speed to go with it.
The two all-engines-operating blocks rest on ratings this engine declares.
Take-off torque and "the maximum speed for use with take-off torque"
[ext CS 27.923(e)] rest on Take-off Power [CS-E 40(a)]. Maximum continuous
torque, and the 75% of it in sub-point (d), rest on Maximum Continuous Power
[CS-E 40(a)]. Both ratings are mandatory for every engine, and the applicant
declares both. The torque and speed limits that go with them reach the
installer through the installation instructions of [[CS-E 20]].

The four conditional blocks divide as follows, against the ratings declared in
`engine_profile.md`.

- **2½ minute OEI power**, sub-point (e)(1). **Not declared.** 2½-Minute OEI
  Power [CS-E 40(b)(3)(iii)] is listed as not claimed, so the 12 runs inside
  the 10-hour take-off block do not arise.
- **30-second and 2-minute OEI power**, sub-point (e)(2). **Both declared**, as
  30-Second OEI Power [CS-E 40(b)(3)(i)] and 2-Minute OEI Power
  [CS-E 40(b)(3)(ii)]. The 10 runs arise.
- **30-minute OEI power**, sub-point (j). **Not declared.** 30-Minute OEI Power
  [CS-E 40(b)(3)(iv)] is listed as not claimed, so the five 30-minute runs do
  not arise.
- **Continuous OEI power**, sub-point (k). **Declared**, as Continuous OEI Power
  [CS-E 40(b)(3)(v)]. The five 1-hour runs arise.

Because continuous OEI power is requested, the reduction in sub-point (d)
applies: the 75% block is 25 hours and not 30 [ext CS 27.923(d)].

One rating name invites a mistake, and the installer has to be told which
rating is meant. The applicant declares Rated 30-Minute Power
[CS-E 40(b)(4)], an all-engines-operating rating limited in use to periods of
no more than 30 minutes. That is **not** 30-Minute OEI Power
[CS-E 40(b)(3)(iv)], which the applicant does not declare. Sub-point (j) is an
OEI sub-point: it asks for runs with one engine made inoperative. A declaration
that names only "30 minutes" would add five single-engine runs that this
installation does not need, and would claim an OEI capability the engine has
not substantiated under [[CS-E 40]].

Two engine-side items feed the 30-second and 2-minute runs. The maximum torque
and the maximum speed for use with each OEI power [ext CS 27.923(e)(2)(i)] come
from the engine's declared limits at those ratings [CS-E 40(b)(3)]. Where a
full-authority EECS sets them, the control function is assessed under
[[CS-E 50]] and its failure behaviour reaches the safety analysis of
[[CS-E 510]].

The bench test relief in (e)(2)(iii) is written around the engine, not the
transmission. It is available "when engine limitations either preclude repeated
use of this power or would result in premature engine removal during the test"
[ext CS 27.923(e)(2)(iii)]. Whether it is available therefore depends on the
usage limits the engine applicant declares for the 30-Second and 2-Minute OEI
Power ratings, and on the inspection or removal action each use triggers. Those
limits are engine data and belong in the installation instructions
[[CS-E 20]].

Sub-point (e)(2)(i) asks for at least one run sequence "from a simulated
'flight idle' condition" [ext CS 27.923(e)(2)(i)], and sub-point (f) fixes the
interval between runs. The idle condition the engine can offer, and the rate at
which it accelerates away from it, are engine data proved under [[CS-E 745]].

The engine's own endurance test is [[CS-E 740]]. It is run on the engine, and
it proves the engine. CS 27.923 is run on the rotorcraft, and it proves the
rotor drive system. Neither schedule substitutes for the other, and the relief
in (e)(2)(iii) exists because the engine may not be able to sustain the
transmission's programme.

Which of the two codes applies is still open. [[CS-E 30]] carries that item, and
the schedules differ enough that the answer changes the run programme entirely.
